title: A Slack channel message claims an issue fixed that never actually closed
author: esu-elegba
description: The first recipe to read a toolkit besides github/x at all -- grepped every one of the 66 existing recipes' own recipe.json toolkit field before writing this one: the set is exactly {github, github+x, x+github}, zero slack, zero gmail, zero anything else, so this is a genuinely new axis, not one more cell in the existing GitHub/X grid. Extracts every real GitHub closing-keyword claim (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses, the shared seam_engine.closing_keywords grammar thirteen sibling recipes already import) from a Slack channel message's own text and cross-checks it against the live issue tracker's own state -- the Slack-side twin of mention-claims-unfixed-issue (the X-mention leg), same seam, different inbound surface: a message posted to a channel, not a tweet or a mention. An issue that exists but is still open is the seam: a message sitting in a Slack channel already disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on either platform ever compares them. Proposed per CONTRIBUTING.md's own 'New toolkits' section, the exact same way gmail_calendar.py proposed gmail/google_calendar before either had a live scope -- fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the message's own ts, holding mention-claims-unfixed-issue's/tweet-claims-unfixed-issue's identical 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number for a new toolkit. A claim checked within 24 hours of posting might still be a race (the real fix landing moments after the message went out) rather than a settled public overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named issue still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-unfixed-issue sibling: the claimed issue's own live state field, verified against ListIssues, not a guess about which tracker the poster meant. A named issue that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future slack-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named issue that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A message with no closing-keyword claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the Slack poster -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
